paper_metadata.title: TERMINAL REMISSION IS POSSIBLE IN SOME PATIENTS WITH JUVENILE MYOCLONIC EPILEPSY WITHOUT THERAPY

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a retrospective cohort from a tertiary referral center, which may introduce selection bias toward more severe or complex cases. While inclusion criteria and baseline characteristics are well-described, the recruitment process (consecutive vs. convenience) is not explicitly stated.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (seizure types and EEG features) were measured using standardized clinical definitions and objective EEG recordings, which were reviewed by multiple experts.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Focal EEG features were defined as regional or lateralized EEG epileptiform patterns. Photoparoxysmal response (PPR) is defined as the occurrence of spikes, spike waves...
items.reasoning: The study provides clear definitions for the primary prognostic factors (EEG patterns).

items.evidence_snippet: All patients were independently evaluated by at least two of the experienced epileptologists during the long-term follow-up.
items.reasoning: Independent evaluation by two experts increases the reliability of the measurements.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is clearly defined with a strict 5-year threshold, which is a robust measure in epilepsy research.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Epilepsy remission at follow-up was defined as a terminal seizure-free period lasting for at least 5 years.
items.reasoning: The outcome is explicitly defined with a temporal threshold.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were divided into three groups: I- fully controlled patients, II- truly resistant patients... III pseudo-resistant patients
items.reasoning: While clinical evaluation is standard, it relies on patient self-reporting of seizures, which is subject to recall bias, though mitigated by the long follow-up.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients were independently evaluated by at least two of the experienced epileptologists during the long-term follow-up.
items.reasoning: The same expert-led clinical evaluation was applied to all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies several confounders (psychiatric disorders, lifestyle) but does not use multivariable modeling to adjust for them simultaneously, relying instead on univariable comparisons.

items.reasoning: The study measured a wide range of potential clinical and demographic confounders.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Psychiatric disorders were found in 41.6% of AED-resistant patients
items.reasoning: While factors are listed, specific diagnostic criteria for 'psychiatric disorders' are not detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders

items.evidence_snippet: The most common reasons for breakthrough seizures reported by the patients were sleep deprivation, stress, alcohol
